facts.raw_span: An 18-month-old girl was brought for evaluation of a swelling in her left medial thigh
the mass had enlarged gradually and was painless, with no history of trauma or infection
a firm, nonpulsatile mass measuring approximately 10 cm, fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin
no signs of inflammation, neurovascular impairment, or inguinal lymphadenopathy
Laboratory tests were unremarkable
a well-defined, lobulated, hypodense mass in the left anteromedial compartment of the proximal thigh
the lesion exhibited internal septations and a density similar to subcutaneous fat
displacing the common and superficial femoral vessels anterolaterally without signs of invasion
it abutted the proximal femoral bone but did not erode it
An MRI confirmed a fatty-appearing, well-circumscribed mass with internal septations
no encasement of neurovascular structures

concepts.why: The mass has a density similar to subcutaneous fat and is well-circumscribed with internal septations, consistent with a lipoma.
The mass is large and has internal septations, which could be consistent with a liposarcoma, although the lack of invasion and erosion of the proximal femoral bone makes this less likely.
The mass displaces the common and superficial femoral vessels anterolaterally without signs of invasion, which could be consistent with a hemangioma.
The mass is fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin, which could be consistent with a neurofibroma, although the lack of neurovascular impairment makes this less likely.
The mass is firm and nonpulsatile, which could be consistent with a fibroma.
The mass has a well-defined border and is lobulated, which could be consistent with a myxoma.
The mass is fixed to underlying tissues but mobile relative to the overlying skin, which could be consistent with a schwannoma, although the lack of neurovascular impairment makes this less likely.
The mass displaces the common and superficial femoral vessels anterolaterally without signs of invasion, which could be consistent with a vascular malformation.

rationales.F02: Painless mass suggests benign tumor, such as lipoma, but does not rule out liposarcoma.
rationales.F03: Firm, nonpulsatile mass is more suggestive of lipoma than liposarcoma or vascular malformation.
rationales.F06: Well-defined, lobulated mass is more characteristic of lipoma than liposarcoma.
rationales.F07: Internal septations and density similar to subcutaneous fat are highly suggestive of lipoma.
rationales.F10: Fatty-appearing mass with internal septations on MRI is highly suggestive of lipoma.
